---

Dear Appeals Reviewer,

I am appealing the denial of prior authorization for my partial knee replacement (CPT 27446), which Anthem Blue Cross Blue Shield of Wisconsin denied on 2026-08-14 under reference number POC-2CCDE26A88-23175. The notice states that the imaging findings submitted do not support the medical necessity of the requested procedure. I am asking for reconsideration, because the imaging and clinical records already in my file line up with the plan's own published criteria under the Carelon Joint Surgery guideline. My surgeon, Dr. Marchetti, has documented that this procedure is needed.

Below I have quoted the plan's criteria exactly as they appear in the guideline and matched each one to what my records show.

### 1. The plan's imaging criteria — and what my imaging shows

The policy states:

> "Imaging reports obtained within the past 12 months describing the degree of cartilage damage as determined by either or both of the following methods: X-ray report or provider interpretation of x-rays that utilizes or can be correlated with the Kellgren-Lawrence grading system of osteoarthritis MRI report from a radiologist that utilizes or can be correlated with the modified Outerbridge or similar classification system related to articular cartilage injury and osteoarthritis"

The policy also states:

> "Imaging evidence of significant joint destruction and cartilage loss, defined as diffuse modified Outerbridge grade III – IV or Kellgren-Lawrence grade 3 – 4, isolated to the medial or lateral knee compartment with no degenerative changes in the opposite compartment"

My records show an MRI of the knee dated 2026-07-03 — within the past 12 months — describing **full-thickness cartilage loss in the medial compartment with bone-on-bone apposition, Kellgren-Lawrence grade 4 medially.** That is imaging obtained in the required window, graded on the Kellgren-Lawrence system named in the policy, and at the top of the grade range the policy identifies as significant joint destruction and cartilage loss.

The policy further states:

> "Imaging reports should be thorough and describe the presence or absence of subchondral cysts, subchondral sclerosis, periarticular osteophytes, joint subluxation, avascular necrosis, or bone on bone articulations. The degree of joint space narrowing should also be noted."

My imaging report expressly describes bone-on-bone apposition in the medial compartment, which is one of the specific findings this paragraph asks reviewers to look for.

If the determination turned on a particular element of the imaging criteria — for example, documentation of the opposite compartment, or a measurement addressed by the criteria quoted below — I ask that the plan identify that element specifically, so that Dr. Marchetti can supply the additional imaging description the policy contemplates:

> "For x-ray interpretation, the provider shall submit a detailed imaging description that correlates with clinical findings of the requested procedure. In the absence of a detailed description, the provider may submit a report from an independent radiologist."

I would like to note plainly that the denial notice gives one general sentence about imaging and does not tell me which criterion in the guideline my imaging was found not to meet. I am asking the plan to state that in writing on reconsideration.

### 2. Conservative management

The policy states:

> "Failure of at least 12 weeks of non-surgical conservative management (unless radiographs show Kellgren-Lawrence grade 4)"

My imaging is graded Kellgren-Lawrence grade 4 medially. Separately, my documented conservative care extends well past twelve weeks: **NSAIDs for 8 months with inadequate relief**, a **corticosteroid injection on 2026-06-16 that gave only 3 weeks of partial relief**, and **supervised physical therapy from 2026-05-26 to 2026-07-21 — 8 weeks, 24 visits completed**, focused on quadriceps strengthening and range of motion, documented in the physical therapy discharge note.

That care matches the combination the policy requires:

> "Conservative management 1 must include a combination of strategies to reduce inflammation, alleviate pain, and correct underlying dysfunction, including physical therapy AND at least ONE complementary conservative treatment strategy."

> "Physical therapy requirement includes ANY of the following: Physical therapy rendered by a qualified provider of physical therapy services Supervised home treatment program that includes ALL the following: Participation in a patient-specific or tailored program Initial active instruction by MD/DO/PT with redemonstration of patient ability to perform exercises Compliance (documented or by clinician attestation on follow-up evaluation)"

My physical therapy was supervised and rendered by a physical therapy provider, with 24 completed visits documented in the discharge note — the first option listed.

> "Complementary conservative treatment requirement includes ANY of the following: Anti-inflammatory medications and analgesics 2 Adjunctive medications such as nerve membrane stabilizers or muscle relaxants 2 Intra-articular corticosteroid injection(s) 2 Alternative therapies such as activity modification, and/or a trial period of rest (e.g., from the aggravating/contributing factors), where applicable"

I had **two** of these, not one: 8 months of NSAIDs and an intra-articular corticosteroid injection.

> "Failure of conservative management requires ALL the following: Patient has completed a full course of conservative management (as defined above) for the current episode of care Worsening of or no significant improvement in signs and/or symptoms upon clinical reevaluation More invasive forms of therapy are being considered"

I completed the course. The NSAIDs gave inadequate relief, the injection gave only three weeks of partial relief, and my pain has been progressive over 14 months and is unrelieved by rest. Surgery is the more invasive therapy now under consideration.

### 3. Symptom duration, severity and function

The policy states:

> "Clinical notes describing symptom duration and severity, specific functional limitations related to symptoms, and type and duration of all therapeutic measures provided. If conservative management is not appropriate, the reason must be clearly documented."

> "Reporting symptom severity – Severity of pain and its associated impact on activities of daily living (ADLs) and instrumental ADLs (IADLs) are key factors in determining the need for intervention. For purposes of this guideline, significant pain and functional impairment refer to pain rated at least 3 out of 10 in intensity and associated with inability to perform ADLs and/or IADLs."

My records document **14 months of progressive knee pain, unrelieved by rest**; that **I cannot climb stairs without assistance**; and that **I wake 3–4 times nightly with pain**. On examination there was **positive provocative testing on the affected side and range of motion limited by pain**. If the plan needs my pain intensity recorded as a numeric rating, I will ask Dr. Marchetti's office to provide it.

### 4. Other criteria in the guideline

The guideline also contains the following provisions, which I include so the reviewer can confirm each against my chart:

> "Clinical reevaluation – In most cases, reevaluation should include a physical examination. Direct contact by other methods, such as telephone communication or electronic messaging, may substitute for in-person evaluation when circumstances preclude an office visit. Clinical reevaluation must be done in reasonable proximity to the anticipated date of service such that the patient's condition would be unlikely to change by the date of service."

> "Intact anterior cruciate ligament or documentation of stable knee examination (UKA may done with concurrent ACL reconstruction if all other criteria are met)"

> "Less than 10 degrees of fixed varus deformity for medial UKA"

> "Less than 15 degrees of fixed valgus deformity for lateral UKA"

> "Where there are patient specific modifiable comorbidities that may adversely impact patient reported outcomes or the health status of the patient, a shared decision-making process to discuss these modifiable comorbidities with the patient is strongly recommended and should be documented."

On the last point, my record notes **no active infection, no untreated substance use, BMI 29, and non-smoker**. For the ligament and alignment items, Dr. Marchetti's office can supply the corresponding examination and measurement documentation promptly if the plan tells me those were the basis for the denial. I should also note that the policy excerpts available to me list further conditions that were not reproduced in full, and I am asking the plan to identify exactly which criteria it applied in my case.

### What I am asking for

I ask that Anthem Blue Cross Blue Shield of Wisconsin overturn the denial of CPT 27446 and authorize the partial knee replacement. If the denial is upheld in whole or in part, I ask that you provide, in writing:

1. The specific criterion or criteria from the Carelon Joint Surgery guideline that my records were found not to meet;
2. The specific records or findings that would satisfy that criterion, so my surgeon can submit them; and
3. The credentials and specialty of the reviewer who made the determination.

I understand my appeal must be received by **2027-02-10**, which is 180 days from the date of the denial notice. I am sending this letter to the appeal address printed on my denial letter; I understand I may also submit or check on my appeal at anthem.com, through the Sydney Health app, or by calling the number on the back of my ID card.

Please contact me at the phone number or email above if anything further is needed. Thank you for taking a careful second look at my file.

Sincerely,

**Rowan Delgado**
Member ID: W169631767
Reference number: POC-2CCDE26A88-23175

**Enclosures:**
- Copy of denial notice dated 2026-08-14
- MRI report dated 2026-07-03
- Physical therapy discharge note (2026-05-26 to 2026-07-21, 24 visits)
- Office notes from Marchetti, MD, orthopedic surgery
- Medication and injection records, including corticosteroid injection 2026-06-16
- [Any additional records my surgeon's office provides]
